To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the azimuthal wakenumber spectra of the acoustic and velocity fields are distinct; (b) the axisymmetric mode is more efficient than the first helical mode at radiating sound; (c) there is significant correlation, as high as ten percent, between the axisymmetric mode and acoustic pressure; (d) linear PSE solutions for the axisymmetric and first azimuthal modes of the velocity agree with the experimental data, and these are likely to be associated with the sound radiation
the azimuthal wavelike features in the velocity field are associated with the low-angle sound radiation.
the low-angle sound radiation of subsonic jets can be associated with wavepackets in the azimuthal modes 1 and 0 of the velocity field.
In summary, our research is concerned with
wavepacket structures of turbulent jets.
the development and application of novel experimental techniques to investigate the relationship between coherent structures in the velocity field and the radiated sound of subsonic jets.
the relationship between the velocity field of a jet and the low angle sound radiation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the velocity field of a turbulent jet can be described as a superposition of wavepackets, the axisymmetric and first azimuthal mode of which are the most relevant to the low-angle sound radiation.
the axisymmetric and first azimuthal modes of the velocity are linear wavepackets and are the dominant source of sound radiation in low angle jets.
the low-angle sound radiation of subsonic jets can be associated with the linear evolution of axisymmetric and first azimuthal modes of the velocity fluctuations in the initial mixing layer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, in spite of the fact that the velocity field is turbulent, the evolution of its azimuthal modes can be described by linear PSE, at least for the first two modes, and these modes are associated with the radiated low-angle sound.
the axisymmetric mode is the most efficient mode in the jet flow, which radiates most sound.
, for the subsonic jets studied here, the low-angle sound is predominantly axisymmetric, and the axisymmetric mode is associated with linear wavepackets that are amplified by the shear layer.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in subsonic, turbulent jets, the axisymmetric and helical modes of velocity and sound can be modelled by linear wavepackets.
linear wavepackets in turbulent jets are associated with low polar angles, which are of primary importance for jet noise reduction.
wavepacket theory can be used to predict the evolution of the axisymmetric and helical velocity field modes of a turbulent jet, and these modes can be used to explain the low angle sound radiation.
